method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: ⚠️ **FB in the larynx or trachea is potentially life-threatening and needs immediate emergency airway management.**
claims.source_text: Inhalation of a foreign body (FB) into the trachea or larynx is a potentially life-threatening event requiring immediate emergency airway management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Often unwitnessed — keep a high index of suspicion** in young children with respiratory symptoms, and **ask specifically about choking**, which may have been days or weeks before.
claims.source_text: FB inhalation is frequently unwitnessed and so a high degree of suspicion is required in young children with respiratory symptoms … A history of inhalation or choking must specifically be sought by clinicians, and may have occurred days or weeks before presentation with symptoms
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most events are in children under 4 years**, commonly nuts, raw carrot or apple, seeds, popcorn, coins, balloons and toy pieces. Older children with developmental impairment remain at risk.
claims.source_text: The vast majority of FB inhalation events occur in children under 4 years and are commonly due to nuts, raw carrot or apple, seeds, popcorn, coins, balloons and pieces of toys. Older children with developmental impairment may continue to be at risk
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Most inhaled FB lodge in the bronchi**, not the larynx or trachea.
claims.source_text: Most inhaled FB are located in the bronchi rather than the larynx or trachea
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Larynx/trachea:** sudden catastrophic event — coughing, choking ± vomiting, severe respiratory distress, stridor, cyanosis, altered mental state, drooling and voice change. **Total obstruction rapidly progresses to unconsciousness and arrest.**
claims.source_text: Impaction in larynx or trachea Sudden and catastrophic event Coughing, choking ± vomiting Severe respiratory distress Stridor Cyanosis Altered mental state Drooling and voice changes Total obstruction will rapidly progress to unconsciousness and cardiorespiratory arrest
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider FB in a child in cardiorespiratory arrest who is impossible to ventilate.**
claims.source_text: May be present in a child in cardiorespiratory arrest who is impossible to ventilate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Main bronchus:** witnessed choking, coughing or wheeze while eating or playing (many unwitnessed), tachypnoea and distress, cyanosis, **persistent wheeze (may be focal and partly bronchodilator-responsive)**, persistent cough, fever, haemoptysis, recurrent or persistent consolidation. May be asymptomatic until complications (pneumonia, abscess, bronchiectasis).
claims.source_text: Impaction in main bronchus Witnessed episode of choking, coughing or wheezing while eating or playing (many are unwitnessed) Tachypnoea and respiratory distress Cyanosis Persistent wheeze (may be focal and partially respond to bronchodilators) Persistent cough Fever Haemoptysis Shortness of breath Recurrent or persistent consolidation May be asymptomatic after initial event before developing complications (pneumonia, abscess, bronchiectasis etc)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examination may be normal.** Look for asymmetrical chest movement, tracheal deviation, focal wheeze or decreased breath sounds; **observe and maintain the child's preferred position** (e.g. sniffing or tripod).
claims.source_text: Examination may be normal Observe (and maintain) child’s preferred position eg sniffing or tripod … Asymmetrical chest movement Tracheal deviation Focal wheeze or decreased breath sounds
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check ears, nose and throat for other FB**, only if the child is stable.
claims.source_text: Check for other FB in ears, nose and throat (if child is stable)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Resuscitate first if needed. Observe every child closely until the FB is removed** — any movement of the FB can cause sudden airway compromise.
claims.source_text: If required provide emergency resuscitation prior to other management. Ongoing close observation is required in all children until FB removed, as any movement of FB may cause sudden airway compromise
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A normal CXR does not exclude it** — there may be no air trapping and most objects are radiolucent. Consider CXR ± inspiratory/expiratory films (if the child can cooperate) or lateral decubitus views.
claims.source_text: Normal CXR does not exclude FB inhalation as there may not be signs of air trapping, and most commonly inhaled objects are radiolucent … Consider CXR ± inspiratory and expiratory films (in children able to cooperate) or lateral decubitus views
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Look for:** radio-opaque FB, segmental or lobar collapse, distal hyperinflation from air trapping, mediastinal shift, consolidation, pneumothorax. **Abscess and bronchiectasis signal a chronic impacted FB.**
claims.source_text: Radio-opaque foreign body Segmental or lobar collapse Hyperinflation distal to obstruction causing air trapping Mediastinal shift Consolidation suggestive of pneumonia Pneumothorax Pulmonary abscess and bronchiectasis are signs of a chronic impacted FB
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **CT is not recommended** — bronchoscopy is likely to be needed; seek expert advice.
claims.source_text: CT is not recommended as bronchoscopy is likely to be required; seek expert advice
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Removal attempts and advanced airway management** (laryngoscopy, Magill forceps, cricothyroidotomy) should ideally be done by a clinician familiar with them — but **a less experienced clinician may reasonably proceed if the child is deteriorating.**
claims.source_text: Attempts at removal of a FB +/- advanced airway management using laryngoscopy, Magill forceps, cricothyroidotomy and other procedures in the flowchart should ideally be performed by a clinician familiar with their use. However, it may be reasonable for a less experienced clinician to proceed if a child is deteriorating.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If attempting these is not safe, continue basic resuscitation while awaiting senior help.**
claims.source_text: If it is not felt to be safe to attempt these procedures, basic resuscitation should be continued while awaiting senior assistance
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Stable airway with ongoing suspicion: refer to ENT or respiratory for consideration of bronchoscopy.** Keep a low threshold for consultation.
claims.source_text: In children who have a stable airway where there is ongoing suspicion of an inhaled FB after history and assessment, refer to ENT or respiratory team for consideration of bronchoscopy Maintain a high index of suspicion with a low threshold for consultation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult ENT or respiratory for any suspicion of an inhaled FB.** Transfer if local services can't perform the procedures or investigations.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with ENT or respiratory team when Any suspicion for inhaled FB … Consider transfer when Local services unable to perform procedures or investigations
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Discharge when the FB is removed and/or the child is stable after a period of observation.**
claims.source_text: FB removed and/or child stable after period of observation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Children under 5 are at greatest risk, especially from food.** Don't offer hard round foods — popcorn, hard lollies, uncut grapes, peanuts or other nuts, raw carrot or apples.
claims.source_text: Children aged under 5 years are at the greatest risk of inhaled foreign bodies, especially food Young children should not be offered hard round foods such as popcorn, hard lollies, uncut grapes, peanuts or other nuts, raw carrot or apples
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sit calmly while eating, one piece of food at a time; avoid toys with small parts under age 3.**
claims.source_text: Encourage children to always sit calmly while eating, and offer food one piece at a time Avoid toys with small parts for children under the age of 3 years
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Foreign bodies inhaled' (Last updated March 2021), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Foreign_bodies_inhaled/, retrieved 2026-09-23
